sections.h2: What should I know about Eden Prairie before I sell my house?
sections.html:
Eden Prairie is a Hennepin County suburb on the north bank of the Minnesota River, about 12 miles southwest of downtown Minneapolis. The Census Bureau counts 63,075 people there for July 2025, which is 1.7 percent fewer than the 2020 base, so the city is no longer in the fast-growth phase that built most of its houses.

That growth came in a short window. The population was 1,384 in 1950, 16,263 in 1980 and 39,311 in 1990. A large share of the homes you will compete with, and the ones buyers compare yours to, were built in those decades.

  • Land area is 32.52 square miles, with rolling hills and bluffs above the river, plus lakes such as Staring Lake, Round Lake and Bryant Lake.
  • The city lists more than 170 miles of trails and 2,250 acres of parks, which buyers treat as part of the property.
  • Main routes are Interstate 494, U.S. 169, U.S. 212 and Minnesota Highway 5.

sections.h2: Who buys houses in Eden Prairie, and what do they pay for?
sections.html:
Buyers here are mostly households tied to the city's employers and its school district. The city's 2024 economic snapshot lists Optum at 6,500 employees, C.H. Robinson at 2,500, Starkey at 2,117, UNFI at 1,600 and the school district at 1,285.

The Census figures for 2020 to 2024 show what that looks like at home: 76.1 percent of households own, the median owner-occupied value is $473,900, and median household income is $130,489. Median gross rent is $1,833, which matters if you are thinking of renting the house out instead of selling. About 64.9 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or more.

A typical Eden Prairie buyer therefore expects a house that looks finished. Deferred maintenance, dated kitchens and unpermitted work are what push owners toward a direct sale to a cash buyer rather than a months-long listing.

sections.h2: Which schools serve Eden Prairie homes?
sections.html:
Eden Prairie Schools serves the city with six elementary schools (pre-K to grade 5, one with Spanish immersion), one middle school for grades 6 to 8 and Eden Prairie High School, which has roughly 2,600 students. Families may also use Minnesota open enrollment to attend a school in another district.

Private and charter options include The International School of Minnesota and the Performing Institute of Minnesota Arts High School. Hennepin Technical College has a campus in the city. For a seller, the practical point is that school boundaries are a fixed selling feature, so name the district in your listing or your conversation with a buyer.

sections.h2: What does Minnesota require me to disclose when I sell in Eden Prairie?
sections.html:
Written disclosure comes first. Before you sign a purchase agreement, Minnesota Statutes 513.55 requires you to tell the buyer in good faith about material facts you know that could significantly affect an ordinary buyer's use and enjoyment.

  • Radon: Section 144.496 requires any test results, mitigation details, the state warning statement and the Department of Health booklet.
  • Wells: Section 103I.235 requires either a statement that you know of no wells or a disclosure of each one.
  • Sewage: Section 115.55, subdivision 6 requires you to say whether sewage goes to a permitted facility.

Give all three in writing with the purchase agreement. Your title company or agent can supply the standard Minnesota forms.

sections.h2: Do I need to worry about permits and unfinished work?
sections.html:
Yes, because Eden Prairie building inspectors treat permits as a record the next owner can read. The city states that building permits expire if there has been no work or inspection for 180 days, that a shed over 200 square feet needs a permit, and that a retaining wall taller than 4 feet needs both a permit and engineering.

A homeowner who lives in the house may do their own work, but permits are still required, and natural gas work is the exception to that allowance. The city also notes that Minnesota law requires residential builders, remodelers and roofers to hold a state license, which you can check through the Department of Labor and Industry.

If your basement finish, deck or roof was done without a permit, ask the city's building inspections office what it would take to close the permit. Starting January 1, 2027, the city adds a 2.95 percent fee ($2.95 minimum) to card payments for permits, while EFT and ACH payments are exempt.

sections.h2: Can I rent my Eden Prairie house instead of selling it?
sections.html:
You can, but the city requires every rental property to be licensed and inspected annually. The Rental Housing line is 952-949-8373. Owners who are weighing a rental against a sale should compare the license, annual inspection and any repair orders against a quick closing.

The city also publishes a Housing Rehabilitation Loan Program and a First Time Homebuyer Program. If your buyer is a first-time purchaser, those pages explain what the city offers, and you can ask the Housing and Community Services office at 952-949-8394 how a sale would interact with them.

sections.h2: What happens with property taxes and recording when my Eden Prairie house sells?
sections.html:
Taxes are billed by Hennepin County and are due May 15 and October 15, moving to the next business day when the date falls on a weekend or holiday. Late payments carry penalties under Minnesota Statutes 279.01. Hennepin's property tax line is 612-348-3011.

The city assessor mails a Notice of Valuation and Classification in early March each year. Eden Prairie says an appraiser verifies physical details at least once every five years.

At transfer, a Certificate of Real Estate Value must be filed with the county auditor for sales above $3,000 under Section 272.115, and state deed tax is 0.33 percent of net consideration under Section 287.21. Your buyer does not inherit your homestead status. Eden Prairie's FAQ says the buyer must apply in their own name after purchase, and the classification is removed for the next assessment year unless they qualify.

sections.h2: What are my ways to sell a house in Eden Prairie?
sections.html:
There are three common routes, and the right one depends on the house's condition and how soon you need to close.

  • List with an agent: best for a clean, updated house when you can wait through showings and buyer financing.
  • Sell it yourself: saves a commission, but you carry the disclosures, paperwork and pricing.
  • Take a cash offer: a buyer purchases the house as it stands, so you skip repairs and showings. Compare the number against your net from a listing, after repairs and carrying costs.

With a median value near $474,000, even small percentage differences are real money, so get at least two figures before you choose.

faqs.q: How fast can I sell my house in Eden Prairie?
faqs.a: It depends on the route. A listing with a financed buyer usually runs through inspection and loan approval, while a cash purchase can close on a date you choose once title work is clear. The county recorder and your title company set the practical floor for the deed to be recorded.

faqs.q: Do I have to fix my Eden Prairie house before selling?
faqs.a: No. Minnesota requires disclosure of material facts you know, not repairs. Open or expired permits are the exception worth checking, since the city keeps permit records a buyer can review, and a permit that lapsed after 180 days of inactivity may need to be renewed.

faqs.q: Does my homestead status transfer to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. Eden Prairie's FAQ says homestead classification is not transferred by the seller. The buyer applies after purchase, and Hennepin County takes applications in person at a service center or online.

faqs.q: What taxes come up at an Eden Prairie closing?
faqs.a: State deed tax of 0.33 percent of net consideration is due when the deed is recorded, and a Certificate of Real Estate Value goes to the county auditor. Your purchase agreement and title company decide how property tax is prorated between you and the buyer.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Eden Prairie house that has tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. The rental must carry the city's license and annual inspection, so call 952-949-8373 to confirm its status before you list. Ask your title company how the tenant's lease and deposit are handled at closing.
